vocabulary.example: The monoblock chair is so ubiquitous that it can be seen in various locations around the world.

vocabulary.definition: the defining spirit or mood of a particular period of history as shown by the ideas and beliefs of the time
vocabulary.example: The Vassili chair reflects the zeitgeist of its era with its design inspired by bicycle production.

vocabulary.definition: able to be maintained at a certain rate or level without causing damage to the environment or depleting resources
vocabulary.example: The monoblock chair has faced criticism for not being a sustainable design due to its mass consumption and lack of individuality.

vocabulary.definition: the process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale
vocabulary.example: The monoblock chair is often cited as an example of globalization due to its widespread presence across different countries.

vocabulary.definition: the gradual development of something, especially from a simple to a more complex form
vocabulary.example: The design of the monoblock chair has evolved over time, becoming thinner, more durable, and cost-effective.

vocabulary.definition: the circumstances that form the setting for an event, statement, or idea, and in terms of which it can be fully understood and assessed
vocabulary.example: Our perception of the monoblock chair design depends on the context in which we encounter it and our prior knowledge of its history.
